plan.title: Genotype x drug interaction: DESeq2 + fgsea in brain RNA-seq
plan.analytical_narrative: The question — does the drug act differently in KO than WT — is an interaction question in a 2x2 factorial (genotype: WT/KO; treatment: vehicle/drug; n=4/cell, 16 samples total, 12000 genes, salmon-derived raw counts). This requires fitting DESeq2 with design ~genotype+treatment+genotype:treatment, testing the interaction coefficient (genotype:treatment) directly, then reporting the two simple effects (drug-vs-vehicle in WT; drug-vs-vehicle in KO) so a reader can see both whether the drug does anything in either genotype and whether that response differs. QC first establishes whether samples cluster by genotype/treatment or show confounds/outliers. LFC shrinkage uses ashr (the interaction and difference-of-simple-effects contrasts are not single coefficients, so apeglm does not apply per the knowledge base). Enrichment runs fgsea preranked on the Wald statistic against MSigDB Hallmark, then Reactome and WikiPathways (all present in the reference store, human, matching organism), once per contrast (interaction + two simple effects), never pooling contrasts. A TF-activity step (decoupler ulm + CollecTRI, both confirmed present) adds a complementary regulator-level view of what drives the interaction, since the research question is fundamentally about a differential transcriptional response. All multiple testing is BH-corrected within each contrast at alpha 0.05 with independent filtering on. The interaction coefficient itself has low power at n=4/cell (difference-of-differences with large SE) — this is stated explicitly rather than glossed over.
